One-class classification for detecting lane departure warning activation traces in sensor streams via autoencoder-integrated density estimation
abstract: The utilization of automated event detection methods enhances surveilling the operation of technical systems via sensor data. Particularly within the automotive domain, there exists an exigency for methodologies that discern events embedded within sensor data. In active vehicle safety systems, diverse driving scenarios are simulated, encompassing scrutiny of vehicle dynamics evaluated by external sensors. Therefore, automated detection methods expedite evaluation by eliminating the need for human-based assessments. This study investigates an event detection method to identify activation intervals of the Lane Departure Warning function within sensor data. The proposed model segments the sensor-driven data based on predefined window and step sizes, subsequently generating scalograms from temporal segments. Scalograms exhibiting significant overlap with the target event are labeled as target scalograms. The model comprises an autoencoder network integrated with a density estimation function. The autoencoder undergoes training to reconstruct target scalograms. The encoder module serves as a mechanism for extracting features from training data, which act as inputs for the density function. The algorithm's effectiveness is determined by evaluating its ability to distinguish the target scalograms from those generated from all temporal segments of unseen sensor data. The algorithm, evaluated on unseen datasets, achieves a precision rate of 94% in pinpointing the event's location, with a time interval offset averaging 0.5 s. This study demonstrates the potential of employing one-class classifiers—traditionally used for anomaly detection—for event detection within sensor data of active vehicle safety experiments. It further highlights that their performance can be enhanced by integrating multiple complementary models.

Data-driven cycle time optimisation in semiconductor manufacturing using machine learning and heuristic search algorithms
abstract: In semiconductor wafer fabrication, cycle time strongly affects throughput and cost, yet is hard to control because bottlenecks shift across tools over time. This paper presents a hybrid framework that combines machine learning (ML) and heuristic optimisation to minimise the imposed Delta Cycle Time (ΔCT) in a wafer fabrication plant. Multiple ML models were trained to predict ΔCT from each tool's Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), and Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO), and Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) were used to optimise these indicators against the trained model. The Random Forest model demonstrated greater robustness than the other Machine Learning models, achieving a best-case per-tool root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.029, although the cross-validated RMSE varies widely across tools (median ≈ 0.49). The framework was evaluated on proprietary data from a Seagate Technology wafer fabrication facility comprising 96 tools. The Random Forest with the Genetic Algorithm achieved the greatest improvement, reducing average ΔCT from +0.276 to −0.392 days (a 0.668-day mean reduction), improving all 96 tools. PSO was comparable at −0.347 days, a 0.623 day reduction, again improving all 96 tools; SQP was more conservative at +0.091 days, a 0.184 day reduction, improving 77 of 96 tools. In some tools, baseline ΔCT is close to zero, so absolute day reductions are a more appropriate indicator than percentage reductions. This framework converts production logs into tool-specific KPI recommendations, showing where cycle-time reductions are achievable.

An engineering-oriented data-to-deployment framework for reliable surface defect detection of annular industrial parts
abstract: Reliable surface defect detection of annular industrial parts remains challenging in practical manufacturing environments due to curved geometries, reflective metallic surfaces, and severe data redundancy caused by continuous rotational scanning. Since adjacent frames contain highly overlapping visual information, conventional random splitting may cause rotational data leakage and overestimated performance. To address these issues, we propose an engineering-oriented data-to-deployment framework that applies lightweight deep learning to automated surface defect inspection. The framework integrates physics-guided data engineering, leak-aware evaluation, geometry-constrained annotation, lightweight detector design, and practical system deployment. First, a physics-based Sector Split strategy reduces the risk of rotational data leakage and aligns evaluation with the physical acquisition process. A geometry-constrained annotation tool further improves labeling consistency across consecutive rotational frames. Second, a Spatial-background suppression, Group-shuffle fusion, and Strip-attention enhanced You Only Look Once detector (YOLO-SGS) is developed for defect localization on reflective metallic surfaces. YOLO-SGS achieves 84.6% mean average precision at 50% intersection over union (mAP@50) with a model-only inference latency of 6.73 ms and 23.3% fewer parameters than the baseline detector. Five-fold physical-part-level cross-validation yields 81.2 ± 1.9 % mAP@50. On three unseen physical parts, the Sector Split model achieves 81.9% mAP@50, compared with 69.0% for the Random Split model. Finally, the AnnularInspector software system is implemented using an asynchronous multi-threaded architecture and achieves a mean end-to-end latency of 494.3 ms with no observed frame loss. External validation and industrial-interference tests further support cross-part generalization within the investigated setting and practical applicability under representative industrial disturbances.

Exploiting surviving features: Interpretable fragmented bamboo slips character recognition via prototype-based vision transformers
abstract: Bamboo and wooden slips (Jiandu) character recognition is challenged by irregular handwriting, unstandardized variants, and diachronic evolution. Moreover, prolonged burial and excavation damage often result in highly fragmented characters with significant morphological variability. With their pictographic structures shattered, recognition depends entirely on incomplete surviving features, making this task significantly harder than identifying intact ancient characters. This motivates the need to fully exploit the limited surviving features of fragmented characters to obtain recognition evidence from known intact characters, while accounting for the label ambiguity caused by severely incomplete and visually indistinguishable character structures. To address these challenges, we propose an interpretable prototype-based Vision Transformer (ProtoViT-FC) that establishes fragment-to-intact associations and incorporates ambiguity-aware supervision. Our model employs contrastive learning to bridge the representational gap between fragmented and intact characters. To mitigate the inherent label ambiguity of incomplete characters, we design two soft-labeling strategies and incorporate the Gradient Harmonizing Mechanism (GHM) loss, enabling the model to predict probable categories from partial features. Additionally, we generate a large synthetic dataset via Fourier-based irregular breakage simulation to address data scarcity. Comprehensive experiments on the large-scale simulated dataset demonstrate that ProtoViT-FC consistently outperforms existing baselines, with paired bootstrap analysis confirming statistically significant improvements across nearly all comparisons. Beyond this specific application, the proposed framework provides a preliminary engineering reference for recognition tasks involving incomplete and ambiguous visual evidence by integrating intact-reference matching, ambiguity-aware supervision, and scalable degradation simulation.

Vision-language sample scoring with dynamic coverage-centric strategies
abstract: Data pruning reduces image-classifier training cost by replacing a full training set with a coreset. Existing methods often require training a target or proxy model to estimate sample importance, which ties data selection to a particular architecture. In addition, common allocation rules do not explicitly change the selected score distribution with the retention budget. We study how to select a fixed-size subset before target-model training while enabling score reuse across architectures and budget-dependent allocation. For this image-classification data-pruning task, we use a frozen Contrastive Language–Image Pre-training (CLIP) encoder as the artificial-intelligence component of a two-stage framework. CLIPSelector computes a two-prompt image-label alignment probability for each training image without optimizing a target or proxy classifier. Dynamic Coverage-centric Coreset Selection (DCCS) partitions the ranked scores into equal-count strata, allocates the initial budget to higher-scoring strata, and samples the remaining budget from a merged lower-scoring region using importance-weighted and uniform probabilities. Experiments on three image-classification benchmarks show that CLIPSelector-DCCS achieves the best average rank among the evaluated methods, generally improves on coverage-centric allocation under matched scoring functions, supports score reuse across target architectures and retention budgets, and reduces downstream training time. Separating score generation from coreset construction enables multiple fixed-budget coresets to be constructed without retraining a scoring model.

title: Blast furnace conditions evaluation and prediction system based on temporal convolutional network
abstract: The accurate analysis and evaluation of the conditions of a blast furnace (BF) is a key problem of intelligent ironmaking, which in turn serves as the basis for the decision-making process regarding the charging of BF. Based on the BF historical charging matrices and conditions data, we develop a BF conditions evaluation and prediction system that is more comprehensive and accurate than the previous models that only consider one or a few individual BF conditions parameters. Firstly, this paper presents the construction of a history database of BF conditions, and innovatively proposes a set of 9-level BF conditions classification method. Secondly, this paper presents a BF conditions evaluation model based on the Temporal Convolution Network (TCN) algorithm. Furthermore, this paper proposes a multi-dimensional temporal convolution network (MD-TCN) algorithm and establishes a BF conditions prediction model. Finally, this paper selects 5 commonly used charging matrices for regulating BF conditions, and selects the most suitable charging matrix for control based on the evaluation of the 5 BF conditions. The simulation results demonstrate that the method proposed in this paper is effective in accurately evaluating and predicting the BF conditions, thereby enhancing product quality and safety.

Data-driven seismic fragility and risk evaluation of existing reinforced-concrete bridge portfolios under limited data
abstract: Preliminary screening of existing transport infrastructure networks is essential to support timely maintenance and retrofit decisions, improve structural resilience, and reduce the economic and environmental impacts of severe damage, failure, and inefficient resource allocation. This study investigates a machine-learning-based pathway for quantitative, simplified seismic risk screening of typologically homogeneous reinforced-concrete girder-bridge portfolios under limited data, in accordance with the Italian Guidelines for existing bridges. Fragility labels are derived through a streamlined cloud-analysis benchmark for 75 simply supported reinforced-concrete lattice-girder bridges, yielding the lognormal fragility parameters: median intensity measure μ , logarithmic dispersion β , and ultimate displacement capacity d u . Supervised regression models are trained to map routinely available inventory descriptors, including geometric and mechanical proxies, to ( μ , β , d u ) . Among the tested models, Gaussian Process Regression provides the best balance between accuracy and stability in the small-sample regime, with cross-validated R 2 values close to 0.9 for all targets. The selected surrogate is applied to 10 additional bridge configurations to assess predictive capability on new cases. Finally, inferred fragility is coupled with site-specific seismic hazard to compute the mean annual frequency of exceedance λ , used to rank 25 bridges of the A19 motorway network in Sicily. Results show prioritization closely consistent with the cloud-analysis benchmark, while requiring substantially lower computational effort. Compared with qualitative guideline-based classes of attention, λ offers useful intra-class granularity for transparent, scalable prioritization. Limitations include reduced accuracy outside the training manifold, typology-specific validation, and lack of explicit condition and defectiveness features.

A physics prior-guided dual-stream attention network for motion prediction of elastic Bragg breakwaters
abstract: Accurate motion response prediction for elastic Bragg breakwaters is critical for their structural safety and operational integrity in marine environments. However, conventional deep learning models often exhibit limited generalization capabilities when presented with unseen sea states. These deficiencies stem from the neglect of natural decay observed in marine systems and inadequate modeling of wave-structure interaction (WSI). To overcome these challenges, this study proposes a novel Physics Prior-Guided Dual-Stream Attention Network (PhysAttnNet). First, the decay bidirectional self-attention (DBSA) module incorporates a learnable temporal decay to assign higher weights to recent states, aiming to emulate the natural decay phenomenon. Meanwhile, the phase differences guided bidirectional cross-attention (PDG-BCA) module explicitly captures the bidirectional interaction and phase relationship between waves and the structure using a cosine-based bias within a bidirectional cross-computation paradigm. These streams are synergistically integrated through a global context fusion (GCF) module. Finally, PhysAttnNet is trained with a hybrid time-frequency loss that jointly minimizes time-domain prediction errors and frequency-domain spectral discrepancies. Comprehensive experiments on wave flume datasets demonstrate that PhysAttnNet significantly outperforms mainstream models. Furthermore,cross-scenario generalization tests validate the model's robustness and adaptability to unseen environments, highlighting its potential as a framework to develop predictive models for complex systems in ocean engineering.

Combination of Fourier Neural Operators and Bayesian Neural Networks to identify anisotropic thermal properties of Callovo-Oxfordian claystone from field heating tests integrating surrogate uncertainty
abstract: Reliable characterization of the thermal properties of Callovo-Oxfordian claystone is critical for the long-term safety assessment of deep geological nuclear waste disposal. This work addresses the Bayesian Inference of key parameters, including transversely isotropic thermal conductivity characterized by the perpendicular conductivity, the anisotropy ratio, equivalent density, specific heat capacity using experimental data from two heating experiments TED and ALC1604. For this aim, the forward problem is first modeled with a three-dimensional COMSOL Multiphysics simulation, and synthesis data per experiment are generated to train surrogate models. We evaluate several machine learning surrogates, including classical regression, deep neural networks, Fourier Neural Operators, and Bayesian Neural Networks. Fourier Neural Operators provides accurate deterministic emulation and serves as the baseline surrogate for Bayesian Inference. To overcome the overconfidence inherent in plug-in approaches, we propose uncertainty-aware surrogates by leveraging the predictive distribution of Bayesian Neural Networks. Three strategies are investigated: (i) CES-style likelihood, marginalizing surrogate uncertainty directly in the likelihood formulation, (ii) E-lik, explicitly incorporates surrogate variance in the likelihood function and (iii) E-pos, propagating surrogate uncertainty at the posterior level via mixtures of posteriors. Bayesian inference is performed with Markov Chain Monte Carlo, and results demonstrate that integrating surrogate uncertainty broadens posterior credible intervals, improves calibration, and avoids overconfident estimates compared to deterministic surrogates. Our findings highlight the importance of explicitly accounting for surrogate uncertainty in Bayesian inversion of computationally demanding uncertainty-aware thermal modeling problems and provide a framework for robust parameter identification of host rock in nuclear waste repository safety assessment

Avoid wasted annotation costs in open-set active learning with pre-trained vision–language model
abstract: Active learning (AL) aims to enhance model performance by selectively collecting highly informative data, thereby minimizing annotation costs. However, in practical scenarios, unlabeled data may contain out-of-distribution (OOD) samples, which are not used for training, leading to wasted annotation costs if data is incorrectly selected. Therefore, to make active learning feasible in real-world applications, it is crucial to consider not only the informativeness of unlabeled samples but also their purity to determine whether they belong to the in-distribution (ID). Recent studies have applied AL under these assumptions, but challenges remain due to the trade-off between informativeness and purity, as well as the heavy dependence on OOD samples. These issues lead to the collection of OOD samples, resulting in a significant waste of annotation costs. To address these challenges, we propose a novel query strategy, VLPure-AL, which minimizes cost losses while reducing dependence on OOD samples. VLPure-AL sequentially evaluates the purity and informativeness of data. First, it utilizes a pre-trained vision-language model to detect and exclude OOD data with high accuracy by leveraging linguistic and visual information of ID data. Second, it selects highly informative data from the remaining ID data, and then the selected samples are annotated by human experts. Experimental results on datasets with various open-set conditions demonstrate that VLPure-AL achieves the lowest cost loss and highest performance across all scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/DSBA-Lab/OpenAL.

SmartSwitchLight: Interpretable multi-agent reinforcement learning for adaptive traffic signal control via generative artificial intelligence based supervisory decision making
abstract: Urban traffic signal control must respond to rapidly changing demand caused by commuting patterns, special events, and non-recurrent congestion, yet conventional fixed-time, actuated, and single-agent reinforcement learning (RL) controllers often struggle to adapt across diverse operating regimes. This paper presents SmartSwitchLight, a generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) supervised multi-agent traffic signal control framework for adaptive urban traffic signal control. The implemented GenAI combines multiple specialized deep reinforcement learning (DRL) controllers, each trained for a distinct signal phase configuration, with a large language model (LLM) based meta-controller that selects the most suitable controller according to real-time traffic conditions, profile-based forecasts, historical performance, and contextual information. Rather than directly issuing low-level signal timing actions, the meta-controller performs high-level policy selection and provides interpretable supervisory reasoning for each decision. The proposed system is evaluated in a high-fidelity microscopic simulation environment under a realistic full-day demand profile with strong directional peaks and event-driven fluctuations. Results show that SmartSwitchLight substantially outperforms fixed-time, actuated, and standalone RL controllers. The quarter-hourly switching configuration reduces mean total intersection delay by 94.7% relative to the best fixed-time controller, 87.9% relative to the best actuated controller, and 83.2% relative to the standalone RL controller. The hourly switching configuration achieves corresponding reductions of 92.4%, 82.7%, and 76.0%, respectively. These findings demonstrate that combining specialized RL policies with GenAI-based supervisory decision making can significantly enhance adaptability, robustness, and interpretability in adaptive urban traffic signal control.

Explainable artificial intelligence for deep learning-based delamination detection in Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymer composites
abstract: The heterogeneous and anisotropic nature of Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymers (CFRP) introduces challenges in characterizing failure mechanisms, particularly delamination, in advanced composite engineering structures used across multiple industrial sectors. Although deep learning models, especially Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), have demonstrated high diagnostic performance in Structural Health Monitoring (SHM), their inherent black-box nature limits interpretability and trust, thereby restricting deployment in real-world engineering applications. To address these limitations, this work proposes a methodology that integrates deep learning with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to enable transparent and reliable delamination detection in CFRP structures. The main contribution in Artificial Intelligence lies in the integration of convolutional neural networks with time–frequency representations of guided-wave signals and model-agnostic explainability techniques for intelligent fault detection in composite materials. From an engineering perspective, the proposed approach is applied to SHM and delamination diagnosis of CFRP specimens subjected to fatigue loading in engineering systems using Lamb waves acquired by piezoelectric transducers. The recorded Lamb wave signals were transformed into time–frequency representations and used as inputs to multiple CNN architectures, evaluated under a leakage-controlled, leave-one-cycle-out cross-validation protocol with multi-seed statistical aggregation, achieving accuracy values of up to 95.9% with statistically validated inter-architecture comparisons The explainability analysis highlighted physically meaningful indicators of delamination, such as amplitude attenuation and frequency shifts, demonstrating the potential of the proposed framework as an intelligent decision-support tool for fault detection and monitoring in engineering applications involving composite structures.

Visual swarm navigation via deep reinforcement learning and evolutionary hybrid design
abstract: Swarm robotics presents a robust and cost-effective paradigm for advanced automation in complex, dynamic environments, such as those encountered in search and rescue or environmental monitoring. A fundamental challenge for this field is the data-driven design of decentralized controllers capable of generating emergent collective behaviors. This paper proposes a novel, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven hybrid methodology for the automatic synthesis of swarm robotic controllers for autonomous visual navigation. This approach synergistically combines multi-agent reinforcement learning with neuro-evolutionary strategies, specifically leveraging implementations of the cross-entropy method and the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy to optimize a pre-trained individual navigation policy. The underlying deep architecture is engineered for low-cost, resource-constrained platforms, utilizing a compact neural network that relies exclusively on monocular camera imagery. This vision-based design emphasizes computational and energy efficiency, a critical requirement for practical swarm deployments. Experiments, performed in a high-fidelity physics simulator, demonstrate that the resulting controllers enable robust and scalable collective exploration of diverse indoor environments. The controller trained using our cross-entropy method achieves superior exploration coverage, visiting 36.20% more regions compared to the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy. Critically, our best vision-based policy achieves exploration performance statistically comparable to traditional methods relying on more expensive distance sensors, while delivering a significant 31.40% average reduction in energy consumption. These findings validate an effective and economically viable autonomous control system, establishing a path for deploying highly efficient collective intelligence in real-world engineering applications.

Pipe flow of thixotropic fluids: Experiments, simulations and neural networks
abstract: Thixotropy refers to the time dependent evolution of a material’s microstructure, where structural agglomerates are progressively broken down under shear and rebuild when flow ceases. This study examines how such microstructural dynamics influence the transient pressure response of thixotropic yield stress fluids in laminar pipe flow. Experiments on Laponite suspensions performed with a custom built pipe rig reveal a pronounced decay in pressure drop over time at constant flowrate, reflecting shear induced structural breakdown. Complementary computational fluid dynamics simulations based on the Houska thixotropic constitutive model reproduce the experimental observations and elucidate the interplay between structural breakdown and recovery that governs the evolution of flow. The simulations capture the transition from plug-like to shear thinning dominated velocity profiles as flow rate increases, accompanied by a reduction of unyielded regions. To reduce computational cost, a feed-forward neural network surrogate trained on a limited set of experimental and simulated data accurately predicts the time-dependent pressure drop across a wide range of flow conditions. The integrated experimental, computational, and data driven framework establishes a quantitative basis for modeling and predicting the unsteady transport behavior of thixotropic fluids in pipe flow.

A practical physics-interpretable hybrid framework for generalizable gas turbine modelling via heterogeneous data fusion
abstract: Existing hybrid gas turbine modelling approaches are often accuracy-driven rather than generalizability-driven and provide limited validation of heterogeneous sensor data. This paper presents a practical, physics-interpretable hybrid modelling framework that embeds data-driven characteristic maps into a physics-based component-matching skeleton, while effectively fusing heterogeneous operational data. Accuracy is enhanced through training on operational data, generalizability is maintained by the physics-based skeleton, and interpretability is achieved via transparent component-level modelling. Physical principles are preserved not only through the skeleton and transparent thermodynamic rules but also reinforced via a novel physics-consistent validation rule and physics-based soft sensors. These soft sensors estimate critical unmeasured variables, and the use of industry-standard methods eliminates dependence on computational fluid dynamics (CFD). Heterogeneous operational data are also rigorously validated using a novel physics-consistent rule to address the robust validation gap. The framework is demonstrated on two heavy-duty turbines, SGT5-2000E and GE Frame 9, across varied loads, ambient conditions, fuels, and control scenarios. Generalization tests show strong predictive capability, with Mean Relative Errors up to 1.15% (SGT5-2000E) and 0.9% (GE Frame 9) under extreme exclusions, remaining within acceptable limits. Results demonstrate the model’s versatility as a cost-effective tool for performance analysis, condition monitoring, and turbine optimization.

title: Recursive online learning for stable long-term prediction of turbulent flows
abstract: Accurate long-term prediction of turbulent flows remains a key challenge in data-driven modeling owing to compounding errors during recursive rollout. We propose a recursive online learning (ROL) algorithm that incorporates simulation feedback into the learning process so as to reduce local prediction errors on surrogate-generated states encountered during long-horizon recursive rollout. We validated the ROL algorithm on both statistically stationary and extremely transient turbulent channel flows using several deep learning architectures. The results show that ROL consistently improves long-term stability and accuracy across the tested network architectures, even in a bypass-like transition. Importantly, ROL-enhanced models generalize robustly to strong noise perturbations and to larger domains beyond the training size while maintaining physically consistent turbulence dynamics. In addition, the trained models achieved speed-ups ranging from 33 × to 231 × relative to a graphics processing unit (GPU)-parallelized numerical solver. The proposed method is effective across the diverse network architectures tested, and enables fast and accurate inference, making it useful in scientific simulations that require robust long-horizon predictions.

Speech-guided unmanned aerial vehicle control system based on large language model-structured execution graphs with expert rule constraints
abstract: As the use of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) expands into industrial and safety-critical applications, there is an increasing need for intuitive speech-driven control systems that reduce reliance on predefined command sets or manual interfaces. Natural language instructions, however, often exhibit ambiguity, logical inconsistency, and a lack of structured representation, which limits their direct applicability to UAV operations. This research develops a speech-guided UAV control system that leverages large language models (LLMs) to construct execution graphs from natural language commands, augmented with expert rule validation for reliable and transparent aerial autonomy. These graphs capture semantically organized control sequences and are refined through expert rule constraints that verify logical consistency, eliminate infeasible actions, and resolve dependency issues. The use of in-context learning enables the LLM to generalize across diverse expressions without requiring additional fine-tuning. The system was evaluated through three experiments targeting language understanding, graph structuring, and rule-based validation. It achieved up to 95.4% accuracy on complex spoken commands, structured 1,000 natural instructions into executable graphs with over 98% accuracy, and corrected all structural issues using expert-defined rules. Real-time performance was maintained with an average latency under two seconds. This work establishes a practical framework for integrating LLMs into voice-controlled UAV systems while ensuring robustness through rule-based validation.

title: Adaptive contract net-based ensemble of learning mechanisms and heuristics for autonomous collaborative scheduling of data relay satellites
ContractShield: Bridging semantic-structural gaps via hierarchical cross-modal fusion for multi-label vulnerability detection in obfuscated smart contracts
abstract: Smart contracts are increasingly targeted by adversaries employing obfuscation techniques such as bogus code injection and control flow manipulation to evade vulnerability detection. Existing multimodal methods often process semantic, temporal, and structural features in isolation and fuse them using simple strategies such as concatenation, which neglects cross-modal interactions and weakens robustness, as obfuscation of a single modality can sharply degrade detection accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose ContractShield, a robust multimodal framework with a novel fusion mechanism that effectively correlates multiple complementary features through a three-level fusion. Self-attention first identifies patterns that indicate vulnerability within each feature space. Cross-modal attention then establishes meaningful connections between complementary signals across modalities. Then, adaptive weighting dynamically calibrates feature contributions based on their reliability under obfuscation. For feature extraction, ContractShield integrates (1) CodeBERT with a sliding window mechanism to capture semantic dependencies in source code, (2) Extended long short-term memory (xLSTM) to model temporal dynamics in opcode sequences, and (3) GATv2 to identify structural invariants in control flow graphs (CFGs) that remain stable across obfuscation. Empirical evaluation demonstrates resilience of ContractShield, achieving a 89 percentage Hamming Score with only a 1-3 percentage drop compared to non-obfuscated data. The framework simultaneously detects five major vulnerability types with 91 percentage F1-score, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches by 6-15 percentage under adversarial conditions.

title: Robust fault-tolerant control for wastewater treatment processes via integrated adaptive dynamic programming with fault-aware experience replay
abstract: Wastewater treatment is a crucial measure to address water scarcity and water pollution, and various control methods have been proposed for wastewater treatment processes (WWTPs). However, actuator faults can compromise existing control strategies and destabilize the system. In this article, an integrated adaptive fault-tolerant control method with improved experience replay is developed for WWTPs. First, an integrated adaptive dynamic programming with fault-aware experience replay (IADP-FAER) is designed. Based on the IADP-FAER, a robust fault-tolerant control framework is established for WWTPs. It utilizes a dynamic weight allocation mechanism to seamlessly integrate the priori knowledge of the original controller into the adaptive dynamic programming (ADP) design, thereby avoiding control conflicts and providing a stable learning environment under actuator faults. Second, the cost function considering actuator faults is constructed for the fault-tolerant controller. The exploration policy obtained from the cost function can effectively suppress adverse effects of actuator faults. The critic and action networks can be established using radial basis function neural networks, which aims to approximate the cost function as well as exploration policy. Their parameters are adaptively adjusted via the policy iteration algorithm so that the control performance of the system is continuously optimized. Third, to further reduce the tracking error and improve the data usage efficiency, a fault-aware experience replay (FAER) is adopted to further adjust the parameters of the networks. By focusing on data with fault features, it allows the controller to quickly adapt to actuator faults. Finally, through simulation experiments, the feasibility of the fault-tolerant control is confirmed.​

Three-dimensional cementing displacement efficiency prediction based on domain-decomposed physics-informed neural network
abstract: Efficient displacement of drilling fluid by cement slurry is essential for ensuring cementing quality, and accurate flow-field prediction is crucial for improving displacement efficiency. Although computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is widely used to investigate displacement mechanisms, high-fidelity three-dimensional simulations are computationally expensive and inefficient for rapid engineering prediction and optimization. In recent years, data-driven neural networks have attracted attention due to their high computational efficiency; however, they rely heavily on large datasets, are prone to overfitting, and may produce predictions that violate physical laws. To address these issues, this study incorporates the governing fluid dynamics equations into the loss function of a deep neural network to impose physical constraints on flow-field evolution. Furthermore, a domain-decomposed physics-informed neural network (DD-PINN) is developed by dividing the computational domain into multiple coupled subdomains. Through parallel training and collaborative solving, the method alleviates convergence difficulties and instability commonly encountered by conventional PINNs in complex three-dimensional flow problems. Numerical experiments based on multi-condition three-dimensional datasets show that DD-PINN achieves higher prediction accuracy for pressure, velocity, and cement slurry concentration fields compared with purely data-driven models. For example, in predicting cement slurry volume fraction, the mean absolute error (MAE) is reduced from 1.27×10⁻² to 2.35×10⁻³. Compared with conventional PINN, the proposed method also significantly improves computational efficiency while maintaining comparable accuracy. Additionally, it enables quantitative evaluation of displacement efficiency and provides guidance for parameter optimization in cementing operations.

Second-order policy gradient methods for the linear quadratic regulator
abstract: Policy gradient methods are a powerful family of reinforcement learning algorithms for continuous control that optimize a policy directly. However, standard first-order methods often converge slowly. Second-order methods can accelerate learning by using curvature information, but they are typically expensive to compute. The linear quadratic regulator (LQR) is a practical setting in which key quantities, such as the policy gradient, admit closed-form expressions. In this work, we develop second-order policy gradient algorithms for LQR by deriving explicit formulas for both the approximate and exact Hessians used in Gauss--Newton and Newton methods, respectively. Numerical experiments show a faster convergence rate for the proposed second-order approach over the standard first-order policy gradient baseline.

A model for the automatic phonemic grouping of Parkinsonian speech
abstract: Parkinson’s disease significantly impacts speech, particularly affecting phonemic groups like stop-plosives, fricatives, and affricates. However, its objective impact on the different phonemic groups has been briefly addressed in the past. This study introduces a new model, called MARTA, built upon a Gaussian Mixture Variational AutoEncoder with metric learning to measure the disease’s impact on the phonemic grouping automatically and objectively. MARTA was trained on normophonic speech before adapting it to parkinsonian speech. The model effectively clusters phonemic groups unsupervised and demonstrates enhanced discriminative power when supervised using forced-aligned labels. Our findings reveal that beyond the traditionally affected phonemes, Parkinson’s disease not only affects stop-plosives, voiced-plosives, and nasals, but also significantly impacts liquids, vowels, and fricatives, with the model achieving a benchmarking 91 % ± 9 discrimination capability. An in-depth evaluation of the impact of the disease on the different phonemic groups represents an advance in the current knowledge of its effects on speech, and has clear implications in the speech therapy of people with Parkinson’s disease. Moreover, regardless of the specific application domain presented, the model introduced has potential downstream utility in assessing the manner of articulation, whether influenced by other medical conditions or certain dialectal variations.

Safe and optimal trajectory learning for autonomous racing via Deep Reinforcement Learning and Control Barrier Functions
abstract: This paper presents a safety-certified learning-based control framework for autonomous racing focused on minimum-time trajectory execution under strict safety and velocity constraints. While Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has emerged as a powerful tool for approximating solutions to optimal control problems, learned policies generally lack formal safety and liveness guarantees, often leading to brittle behavior and constraint violations, especially outside the training distribution. We propose a multi-stage architecture in which a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) policy learns to optimize racing performance, while a filtering stack enforces safety and feasibility by construction. The framework combines a Control Barrier Function (CBF) safety filter with a feasibility-correction mechanism and a Control Lyapunov Function–based tracking controller. The path-dependent CBF encodes track limits around the geometric centerline, allowing dynamically feasible deviations while maintaining safety during training and deployment. By restricting exploration to admissible regions, the filter improves learning stability and prevents the failure modes observed in unconstrained DRL. The policy is trained on a single track and evaluated on 23 1:10-scale tracks, including 22 unseen during training. The proposed method achieves consistent completion on all 23 tracks, whereas the otherwise equivalent unfiltered policy does so on only two. It also achieves lower mean lap times than a classical path-following controller on 22 of the 23 tracks and than Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) on all 23 tracks, reducing average lap time by 4.47% and 1.79%, respectively. These results demonstrate competitive racing performance and zero-shot transfer without offline racing-line optimization.

A cross-scale meteorological-prior-informed adaptive fusion framework for ultra-short-term wind power forecasting
abstract: With the increasing penetration of wind power in electricity grids, accurate wind power forecasting (WPF) has become crucial for maintaining grid stability. Existing data-driven methods, while proficient in nonlinear modeling, are fundamentally limited by a lack of explicit cross-scale meteorological context. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces Global-Regional Cross-scale Meteorological Integration for Wind Power Forecasting (GRCMI-WPF), a cross-scale meteorological-prior-informed adaptive fusion framework that incorporates artificial-intelligence-weather-model-derived atmospheric context from global weather models into local ultra-short-term WPF. Through a dedicated Global-Regional Cross-scale Meteorological Integration (GRCMI) strategy, the framework extracts and injects multi-scale meteorological context surrounding target wind farms as weather-forecast-derived meteorological priors into the forecasting pipeline. Within this framework, we further propose the Dynamic Context-dependent Fusion Network (DCFNet), which employs a Hierarchical Cross-modal Alignment Transformer (HCAT) to effectively mitigate the dimensional and semantic disparities between heterogeneous meteorological priors and power series, and a Dynamic Context-dependent Fusion Gate (DCF-Gate) to adaptively allocate soft weights between historical power and meteorological modalities, achieving context-aware meteorological-prior-informed fusion. Extensive experiments on five real-world wind farm datasets demonstrate that the proposed GRCMI-WPF consistently outperforms the considered contemporary baselines under a unified evaluation protocol, confirming the value of integrating cross-scale meteorological priors for improving local WPF accuracy.

A novel graph reinforcement learning framework for multilevel flexible scheduling in fuzzy production environments
abstract: Existing intelligent optimisation algorithms for fuzzy scheduling often rely on multidimensional, feature-based evaluations of fuzzy numbers, making repeated solution evaluation computationally expensive. This study presents an end-to-end graph reinforcement learning framework for a multilevel flexible manufacturing scheduling problem with fuzzy processing times. The framework jointly models the problem using a multi-attribute hierarchical fuzzy heterogeneous scheduling graph and a fuzzy-aware Markov decision process, with triangular fuzzy numbers represented as node and edge attributes. A fuzzy-aware heterogeneous graph attention network incorporates fuzzy processing times into attention weights through edge feature-enhanced attention and exploits the size-invariant message-passing structure of graph neural networks for cross-scale generalisation. A hierarchically decoupled heterogeneous actor-critic architecture decomposes each scheduling action into stage, entity and machine selection, while adaptive load-balancing guidance and constraint-aware masking support resource allocation and feasibility. Proximal policy optimisation is used as the standard policy optimiser. Experiments are performed to evaluate solution quality, scalability and computational efficiency across multiple instance groups. The proposed framework produces competitive schedules and is approximately 18.6 times faster.

The hidden cost of an image: Quantifying the energy consumption of Artificial Intelligence image generation
abstract: With the growing adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) image generation, in conjunction with the ever-increasing environmental resources demanded by AI, we are urged to answer a fundamental question: What is the environmental impact hidden behind each image we generate? In this research, we present a comprehensive empirical experiment designed to assess the energy consumption of AI image generation through diffusion models. Our experiment compares 17 state-of-the-art image generative models by considering multiple factors that could affect their energy consumption, such as model quantization, image resolution, and prompt length. Additionally, we consider established image quality metrics to study potential trade-offs between energy consumption and generated image quality. Results show that image generation models vary drastically in terms of the energy they consume, with up to a 46x difference. Image resolution affects energy consumption inconsistently: increasing resolution fourfold (from 512 × 512 to 1024 × 1024) yields energy increases ranging from 1.3x to 4.8x across models. U-Net-based models tend to consume less than Transformer-based one. Model quantization instead results to deteriorate the energy efficiency of most models, while prompt length and content have no statistically significant impact. Results show that, albeit not common, an effective trade-off between image generation energy consumption and its quality is possible, with few of the models producing the highest quality images also being among the most energy efficient ones.

Automated measurement of rural highway widths using transformer-based models and point cloud analysis
abstract: This study presents an automated method for extracting roadway width measurements and lane counts from Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR)-derived point clouds of rural highways and evaluates the reliability of measurements obtained from point clouds labeled by a Transformer-based point classification model. The proposed approach was evaluated on five highway segments in Alberta, Canada, encompassing both multilane and two-lane, two-way (TLTW) highways. From an artificial intelligence perspective, the study proposes a hierarchical Transformer-based semantic segmentation strategy with a geometry-aware measurement algorithm to estimate traveled way widths, shoulder widths, and lane counts directly from three-dimensional point cloud data. Automated measurements derived from manually labeled point clouds demonstrated strong agreement with manual reference measurements, with correlation coefficients exceeding 0.99 and mean absolute errors on the order of only a few centimeters for traveled way and shoulder widths. When applied to point clouds automatically segmented by the Transformer-based models, the framework continued to produce reliable results, with width estimation errors generally remaining within sub-meter ranges. Paired statistical tests indicated no statistically significant differences between automated and reference measurements at the 95% confidence level. Multiple lane count estimation strategies were evaluated, with lane-surface-based methods demonstrating increased robustness in scenarios where pavement markings were partially occluded or inconsistently detected. The results confirm that Transformer-based semantic segmentation, when combined with geometry-aware post-processing, can support accurate and scalable roadway geometry extraction from mobile LiDAR data. The proposed framework reduces reliance on manual surveys and offers a practical solution for automated roadway inventory generation and data-driven infrastructure management.

abstract: Accurate prediction of asphalt pavement deterioration is critical for data-driven infrastructure asset management. However, conventional data-driven models commonly provide deterministic estimates, offering limited insight into prediction confidence. This limitation restricts their application in risk-aware decision-making, where understanding the reliability of each prediction is essential. This study addresses this challenge by developing an uncertainty-aware framework for predicting pavement roughness using data from the Long-Term Pavement Performance program. A curated dataset of 1,246 test sections across 50 states in the United States was compiled, covering diverse climate regions, structural configurations, traffic loading, and surface characteristics. Probabilistic modeling approaches, including Bayesian neural networks and Gaussian process regression, were used to predict pavement roughness while generating prediction intervals. Deterministic approaches, including random forest, extreme gradient boosting, support vector regression, and artificial neural networks, were also developed under the same validation and optimization framework for benchmarking. All models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation and optimized using a Bayesian optimization framework. The results showed that extreme gradient boosting achieved the highest point prediction accuracy, while Gaussian process regression and Bayesian neural networks provided competitive accuracy, with coefficients of determination of 0.9133 and 0.9226, respectively, along with explicit uncertainty estimates. Gaussian process regression also demonstrated a reliable uncertainty calibration, with empirical coverage of 95% prediction intervals ranging from 88.89% to 96.31% across climate regions. Initial roughness, rutting, and cracking were identified as the dominant predictors. Regional analyses further revealed generally lower prediction errors in non-freezing regions, and spatial analyses identified geographic variations in pavement deterioration.

title: Safety evaluation of new energy three-electric systems using enhanced physics-informed neural networks

Energy-efficient deep learning-based vibration monitoring on parallel ultra-low-power microcontrollers
abstract: Structural health monitoring (SHM) through vibration analysis is essential for ensuring safety, reliability, and minimized maintenance costs in sensor-connected environments. Realizing this at the extreme edge, directly on sensor nodes, requires advanced data analytics, ultra-energy-efficient hardware, and high-fidelity datasets. This paper addresses these challenges by developing an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based deep learning framework for vibration-based structural health monitoring tailored to resource-constrained devices. We present a benchmarking dataset for vibration SHM, encompassing nine abnormal conditions that capture narrowband structural anomalies. Leveraging this dataset, we design supervised and unsupervised deep-learning models, integrating a system identification (SysId) preprocessing stage to derive structurally informed features that enhance model input quality. This improves algorithmic results while boosting hardware performances. These models are deployed on a parallel ultra-low-power microcontroller with dedicated hardware acceleration. Our unsupervised anomaly detectors deliver 89.90 percent (%) accuracy, 4.1 percentage points higher than the state-of-the-art attention-based baseline, favoring recall and missed-detection reduction at the cost of a higher false-alarm rate while consuming 13 microjoules (µJ) in low-power mode and requiring 370 microseconds (µs) in high-performance mode. This marks one of the first experimental validations of unsupervised on-device vibration diagnostics. Supervised counterparts achieve 96.06 % binary and 91.5 % multiclass accuracy, rivaling Residual Network (ResNet) with 1 5 . 8 × fewer parameters, at less than 235 µJ and not more than 6.3 ms (ms) inference. Relative to existing edge implementations, our approach is one to three orders of magnitude more energy-efficient and two orders faster, unlocking AI-enabled autonomous, low-latency predictive maintenance for large-scale distributed infrastructure monitoring.

Multi-objective optimized signal decomposition with explainable and reliable hybrid models for multistep significant wave height forecasting in ocean wave energy applications
abstract: Accurate forecasting of significant wave height (Hs) is vital for marine safety, coastal engineering, and renewable energy production. This study presents an effective integrated model system to forecast Hs for two distinct sites in Australia, Gladstone and Palm Beach, over various time horizons from 30-min to 24-h ahead during the period of 2018 to 2022. In the first stage, a novel multi-objective Optuna is developed to optimize the decomposition parameters using two criteria of compactness, bandwidth, and peakedness of a signal's frequency spectrum. The proposed methodology is utilized for hyperparameter tuning of Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) and De-mixing Multivariate Variational Mode Decomposition (D-MVMD) techniques. This enables an optimal data decomposition process by eliminating the need for manual parameter selection. In the second stage, an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) approach, SHAPley Additive Explanations (SHAP), is used to identify the most influential components and analyze their interactions. These optimized and interpretable decomposed signals are then used as inputs to standalone forecasting models, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), deep Random Vector Functional Link (RVFL), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). These optimized and interpretable decomposed signals are then used as inputs to the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), deep Random Vector Functional Link (RVFL), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models to forecast. In the final stage, a comprehensive Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) is employed to quantify uncertainties and perform reliability analysis. The SHAP-based feature selection reduced the input variables from 37 to 48 decomposed components to a single dominant predictor while maintaining nearly identical predictive accuracy across all forecast horizons, significantly lowering computational costs. Among the models, the SSA-RVFL demonstrated superior performance, with lower computational cost and the highest forecasting accuracy across all time horizons. This model achieved the highest Index of Agreement (IA: 0.81-1) and determination coefficient (R 2 : 0.49-0.98), and lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE: 0.04-0.33) across stations and horizons. In addition, the results confirm operational reliability exceeding 88% for forecasts up to 6 h ahead. Overall, the fully optimized SSA integrated with the SHAP-RVFL-MCS results provides a robust framework for enhancing decision-making in coastal hazard and wave energy planning.

Transport Layer Security attack detection using hardware performance counters side-channel
abstract: Cryptographic protocols form the backbone of secure communication in various environments, including the Internet of Things (IoT) and non-IoT settings. One of the most popular and widely used cryptographic protocols is Transport Layer Security (TLS). However, TLS implementations remain vulnerable to implementation flaws, such as the Heartbleed bug, which affected a significant proportion of deployed TLS 1.2 servers. Many detection approaches rely on network traffic inspection, which is ineffective in encrypted environments. In this paper, we present a non-intrusive detection framework that collects hardware performance counter (HPC) side-channel data from a TLS server process without modifying the application or requiring access to network packets. To the best of our knowledge, no prior work has combined HPC data with a deep neural network (DNN) in a zero-modification testbed for TLS attack detection. The training dataset was collected in a simplified single-machine setup, while evaluation was conducted on physically separated machines to simulate real-world deployment. Recall ranges from 0.590 to 0.753, and Specificity from 0.698 to 0.850 across six evaluation configurations, confirming the feasibility of detection while identifying generalization as the key challenge for future work. To validate the choice of DNN architecture, it was additionally compared against classical machine learning baselines such as Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), achieving the highest combined Recall and Specificity in all six configurations.

abstract: In the early stages of vehicle development, surrogate models and machine learning play an increasingly important role. In order to optimize the sound in the interior efficiently, engineers use surrogate models of finite element simulations to minimize high-priced hardware tests. Surrogate models based on neural networks have a high demand of time-consuming simulations to provide a sufficient data basis for training, validation, and testing. In this work, simulations from real development processes are used to investigate the methodology of transfer learning to lower this demand. The transfer learning methodology uses a pre-trained neural network of vehicle A to train a surrogate model for vehicle B with significantly less data. The data basis consists of mechanical point admittances from vibroacoustic simulations in the frequency-domain, which characterize the vibration propensity of a structure and describe a typical evaluation parameter in vibroacoustics. We evaluate this methodology of transfer learning for different vehicles based on the performance of the neural networks. With good performance of the transfer learning step, time-consuming finite element simulations can be saved to train surrogate models for vehicle design. To the best of our knowledge, the investigation of transfer learning on time-consuming, real-world production finite element simulations of different vehicles has not been available in the literature yet. Furthermore, this work is characterized by frequency-domain data.

Mechanics-audited stateful operators for path-dependent finite-element digital twins
abstract: Path-dependent finite-element digital twins require predictions of both displacement and hidden plastic state. Accurate fields alone do not establish correct state evolution or mechanical equilibrium. We develop a mechanics-audited graph operator with coupled nodal and quadrature-point recurrent states. The operator predicts the full plane-strain plastic tensor and accumulated equivalent plastic strain, while assembled residuals, native energy, and local constitutive discrepancies regularize training. All core models share an elastic reference. A separate linear snapshot anchor retains the field-versus-mechanics comparison. The benchmark contains 240 independent material and loading trajectories on three complex quadratic meshes, with plastic activation and small-deformation range checks for every reference. Training, validation, and test sets are disjoint; 60 model runs use 50 epochs and five seeds. The 96-trajectory test set includes an unseen non-proportional path family. Against the architecture-matched data-only model, the audited operator changes mean active-state-increment error from 0.651 to 0.702 and residual ratio from 4.102 to 2.142. The joint residual and field-error benefit is not established. The residual-improvement direction persists under classical constitutive reintegration. The main model’s mean displacement relative error is 0.041; paired trajectory intervals and optimization variability are reported separately. Non-recurrent full-prefix and transformer-based constitutive baselines expose the remaining tradeoffs. The results support separate assessment of observable fields, plastic memory, and equilibrium within a qualified numerical domain; they do not establish universal model superiority or autonomous deployment reliability.

Soil property prediction method incorporating spatial variability through local association analysis
abstract: Soil properties are shaped by interacting pedogenic, geological, and environmental processes and exhibit pronounced spatial heterogeneity. With limited and spatially discrete measurements, representing broad spatial trends and localized variations simultaneously remains challenging. Artificial intelligence methods provide nonlinear learning capabilities for integrating spatial and covariate information, but their effectiveness depends on representations that explicitly describe spatial variability. This study proposes a soil property prediction method incorporating spatial variability through local association analysis. The principal contribution is an explicit multi-scale local association representation embedded in deep regression, enabling nonlinear relationships among soil properties, spatial coordinates, local spatial responses, and available covariates to be learned jointly. Spatial centers identified through clustering are used to construct radial basis function features across multiple influence ranges. These features are combined with coordinates and covariates in a deep neural network for prediction and uncertainty quantification at unsampled locations. Validation was conducted using 20 independent random fields and two public European soil data sets representing different sampling patterns and covariate conditions. Across the random fields, the proposed method achieved the lowest mean absolute error among thirteen methods, with reductions of 5.7% to 31.8% relative to the comparison methods. It also achieved the lowest error among the same methods in both measured soil cases. Covariates more strongly associated with the target produced larger accuracy gains, while multi-scale spatial features remained influential when covariates were limited. The proposed method offers an artificial intelligence approach for reliable soil property prediction and engineering geological assessment under complex spatial heterogeneity.

abstract: This paper implements artificial intelligence for month-ahead renewable power forecasting by fusing synchronized solar and wind information from the Sakaka Solar Plant and Dumat Al-Jandal Wind Farm in Saudi Arabia. Ten hybrid deep-learning architectures are evaluated under a common temporal framework using mean absolute error, root mean squared error, mean absolute percentage error, coefficient of determination, training time, and computational carbon dioxide emissions. The convolutional neural network-long short-term memory model with attention achieves the highest predictive accuracy, with a mean absolute error of 80, a root mean squared error of 129, a mean absolute percentage error of 6.6%, and a coefficient of determination of 0.87. The Temporal Fusion Transformer provides the strongest accuracy-sustainability compromise under the 70:30 Sustainable Artificial Intelligence score, while the wavelet-convolutional neural network-gated recurrent unit model records the lowest training footprint at 768 grams of carbon dioxide equivalent. A 10,000-draw perturbation sensitivity analysis of the error and emission values confirms that the preferred deployment model is decision-dependent rather than universally dominant: the Temporal Fusion Transformer is most frequently top-ranked under the central weighting, whereas carbon-heavier or carbon-lighter alternatives become preferred as decision weights change. The contribution is therefore system-level: the framework integrates cross-resource data fusion, leakage-aware long-horizon evaluation, carbon-aware model selection, Pareto analysis, and explicit decision-robustness testing. Reported carbon reductions refer to model computation and should not be interpreted as measured reductions in grid curtailment or citywide operational emissions.

A lightweight deep learning architecture for crack segmentation in structural health monitoring
abstract: Automated crack segmentation is a key component of vision-based structural health monitoring for civil infrastructure. However, many deep learning approaches remain computationally demanding for embedded edge devices and exhibit limited generalisation across diverse materials and imaging conditions. This paper presents a lightweight deep learning architecture designed to balance segmentation accuracy, computational efficiency, and cross-domain robustness. The artificial intelligence contribution is an efficient encoder–decoder integrating depthwise separable convolutions, lightweight multi-scale context aggregation, and channel attention. The proposed approach targets crack continuity through a unified design for thin-structure segmentation under strict computational constraints. The engineering contribution is a practical inspection method for structural health monitoring systems with limited memory, latency, and power budgets. Experiments on a joint dataset comprising 30,017 crack images collected from 20 heterogeneous datasets demonstrate competitive performance across diverse conditions. The proposed Lightweight Attention Channel-Enhanced Crack Segmentation (LACE-Crack) architecture achieves a higher harmonic mean of precision and recall (F1 score) (0.569 vs. 0.566), precision (0.751 vs. 0.732), mean intersection over union (0.694 vs. 0.693), optimal image scale (0.489 vs. 0.480), and optimal dataset scale (0.425 vs. 0.411) than the comparison architecture, with comparable recall (0.459 vs. 0.462). It also requires approximately 43% fewer parameters and 64% fewer floating-point operations. These results demonstrate a strong balance between crack segmentation performance and computational efficiency, supporting the practical use of lightweight artificial intelligence for infrastructure inspection under deployment constraints.

title: Topic-guided artificial intelligence for cybercriminal Telegram identification and classification
A multi-stage graph-conditioned probabilistic forecaster with dual-stream temporal encoding for wind speed forecasting
abstract: Accurate wind speed forecasting is a critical foundation for wind power dispatch and the grid integration of renewable energy. The non-stationary fluctuations in wind speed time series, the spatially dependent variations among multiple wind turbines, and forecasting uncertainties continue to pose significant challenges for wind farm-level forecasting. This paper proposes an artificial intelligence framework for multi-turbine wind speed forecasting, termed the Multi-Stage Graph-Conditioned Probabilistic Forecaster (MGPF).The model fuses prior graphs and data-driven graphs at the node-pair level, enabling differentiated spatial connection representations for different wind turbine pairs. Simultaneously, it sets up two candidate temporal encoding paths, a Generative Pre-trained Transformer 2 (GPT-2) and a lightweight Patch, and determines the appropriate configuration based on comparative results across different datasets. Spatio-temporal cross-attention further establishes interactions between spatial and temporal features, while the probabilistic prediction head constructs prediction intervals by estimating the mean and variance of future wind speeds. Experimental results on two wind farm datasets with markedly different scales show that MGPF reduces the root mean square error (RMSE) by 35.56% and 3.92%, respectively, compared to the corresponding optimal baselines, experiments at the Kelmarsh external wind farm further validate the model's applicability under different wind farm data conditions. Probabilistic forecast results show that MGPF outperforms the probabilistic baseline overall in terms of probability distribution fitting and forecast interval quality, encoder and pre-training control experiments also validate the effectiveness of the time-encoding design.

A diffusion-based generative model for system failure prediction in industrial predictive analytics
abstract: Predicting the time-to-failure (TTF), or remaining useful life (RUL), of engineering assets from degradation signals is central to prognostics and health management (PHM) in aerospace, manufacturing, and energy. Existing methods fall into two families: model-based approaches that impose a parametric degradation trajectory (e.g., Bayesian updating) and data-driven approaches that regress failure time on reduced-dimensional features (e.g., principal component analysis (PCA)-based lognormal regression). Both perform well under smooth, monotonic degradation but degrade under irregular, nonstationary, or multimodal dynamics, and neither provides calibrated uncertainty beyond a single point estimate. We propose a conditional diffusion-based generative model that learns the distribution of future degradation trajectories from a partially observed signal, so that thresholding each generated trajectory yields a full predictive TTF distribution. Two components adapt diffusion to degradation data: a Gaussian-process-correlated forward process that preserves temporal continuity, and a time-aware denoiser that couples a multiscale convolutional encoder–decoder network with a self-attention-based sequence model via cross-attention and dual embeddings of the diffusion step and physical time. On synthetic datasets of controlled difficulty and a public real-world PHM benchmark, the model consistently outperforms both baselines across point, distributional, and trajectory-level metrics, with the largest gains near the failure threshold and under heteroscedastic, multimodal degradation; a controlled comparison further isolates the Gaussian-process-correlated noise as the primary source of this improvement. These results support conditional diffusion as a robust, scalable approach for industrial predictive analytics.

title: A strict safety-guaranteed agentic decision framework for safety-critical industrial systems
abstract: With the advancement of industrial systems toward Industry 5.0, artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded into engineering systems to enable autonomous and adaptive decision-making under dynamic and safety-critical conditions. In such environments, intelligent agents must simultaneously optimize performance and satisfy strict constraints arising from safety, resource limits, and real-time requirements. This paper makes a contribution to artificial intelligence by proposing a Strict Safety-Guaranteed Agentic Decision Framework (SSGAD) that explicitly separates feasibility from performance optimization. A learnable constraint model is developed to estimate unknown system constraints, based on which an uncertainty-aware mechanism constructs a high-confidence feasible action space. Policy optimization is subsequently performed within this learned feasible domain, ensuring that generated decisions satisfy safety and resource constraints while optimizing system performance. The proposed framework is applied to industrial edge scheduling, where multiple heterogeneous nodes cooperatively execute dynamic tasks under resource and latency constraints. Experimental results demonstrate that SSGAD effectively balances performance optimization and safety enforcement. In the stress-load scenario, SSGAD achieves an 84.6% task success rate while maintaining a low violation rate of 9.8%, outperforming existing approaches in safety-critical industrial decision-making.

Structured variational quantum control for spin-chain state transfer: Expressivity, trainability, and robustness
abstract: We propose a hybrid variational framework for quantum optimal control of high-fidelity state transfer in spin chains. The continuous-time control problem is reformulated as a trainable Trotterized quantum circuit, where drift dynamics are encoded by fixed two-qubit interaction blocks and control fields by parameterized on-site R Z rotations. This provides a physics-informed variational ansatz directly connecting the Hamiltonian model to hybrid quantum–classical optimization. We compare two control parameterizations: an expressive local scheme with site-wise trainable parameters and a compact global scheme with shared parameters per Trotter layer. Numerical experiments on XXZ spin chains show that both achieve near-unit fidelity for the main noiseless end-to-end transfer task. The reduced optimization dimension of the global parameterization provides favorable optimization behavior for several larger systems, while additional source–target experiments demonstrate that this advantage is task dependent and that local control can perform better for interior transfers. Studies under depolarizing and dephasing noise show that relative noise-induced degradation depends on system size, noise strength, and noise model, with no uniform robustness ordering. Additional analyses examine circuit depth, initialization sensitivity, empirical gradient statistics, interaction anisotropy, Trotter error, exact piecewise-constant control, and hardware execution. Overall, the results reveal a trade-off between control expressivity, optimization dimensionality, task structure, and noise sensitivity, providing a physically grounded framework for structured variational quantum control of distributed quantum systems.

An optimal non overlapping block diffusion scheme based on genetic algorithm and its application to chaos-based image encryption
abstract: This paper presents an image encryption algorithm based on a novel discrete-time chaotic system and the evolutionary optimization of cryptographic processes. The proposed cryptosystem follows a Confusion-Diffusion-Permutation-Confusion architecture, where confusion is achieved using Arnold transform and permutation relies on the Nanfak permutation technique. The diffusion stage employs a non-overlapping block-based mechanism in which the image is randomly partitioned into k blocks during initialization, while the associated partial diffusion keys are optimized using a genetic algorithm. Unlike conventional key assignment, candidate partial keys are evaluated according to their contribution to the entropy of the globally diffused image, providing an adaptive key-selection mechanism for different image contents. The final confusion stage is independently optimized as a single-objective problem targeting the minimization of inter-pixel correlation under a local Shannon entropy constraint. All pseudo-random sequences involved in the encryption processes are generated using a three-dimensional cross-coupled trigonometric modular hyperchaotic map, which exhibits strong nonlinear dynamic, sensitivity to initial conditions, and suitable sequences for cryptographic applications. The practical feasibility of the chaotic generator is validated through field-programmable gate array implementation on a Cyclone IV DE0-Nano board. Extensive experimental and security analyses demonstrate a large key space, high resistance to statistical attacks and strong robustness against differential attacks. Moreover, the scheme exhibits resilience to noise and clipping attacks, confirming its suitability for secure image transmission.
